category_title: Boys who project personal experiences of physical abuse onto bullying behavior
scenario_title: Role-play activity discussing a bully's intentions and feelings
minimal_context: The student and researcher are participating in an individual 20-minute role-play activity using semi-structured scripts to discuss a bullying incident.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: We are going to do a 20-minute role-play activity using this script and scarf. Let's look at the second part of the script. Who do you think the victim could talk to about the bullying incident?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: He could talk only with his grandparents and his teacher.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: What about the bully? What could be a solution for him?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Apology would be the right thing to do in order to ﬁnd a way out of his problem but at the same time it would be a mistake since by apologising he would show weakness and nobody would hold him in high esteem anymore.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's think about the bully's intentions. Why do you think the bully acted aggressively during the incident?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Maybe his father had hit him that morning and he was so sad …he didn ’t really want to harm the other child.

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: We are going to do a 20-minute role-play activity using this script and scarf. Let's look at the second part of the script. Who do you think the victim could talk to about the bullying incident?

STUDENT: He could talk only with his grandparents and his teacher.

TUTOR: What about the bully? What could be a solution for him?

STUDENT: Apology would be the right thing to do in order to ﬁnd a way out of his problem but at the same time it would be a mistake since by apologising he would show weakness and nobody would hold him in high esteem anymore.

TUTOR: Let's think about the bully's intentions. Why do you think the bully acted aggressively during the incident?

STUDENT: Maybe his father had hit him that morning and he was so sad …he didn ’t really want to harm the other child.

task.content: Responding to questions about a bully's intentions during a 20-minute role-play activity involving semi-structured scripts and monologues about a bullying incident.

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When explaining why the bully might have acted aggressively during the role-play
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Stated that the bully might act in that way because that day he was very sad, and that he didn't really want to harm the other child
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: Projecting his own experience of physical abuse by his father (displacement)
related_quotes: Maybe his father had hit him that morning and he was so sad …he didn ’t really want to harm the other child

behavior_patterns.condition: Identifying potential people the victim could talk to during the second part of the role-play activity
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Said that the victim could talk only with his grandparents and his teacher, since the boy's grandparents were his shelter when his father got angry with him
behavior_patterns.internal_state: Seemed to have a very close relationship with his teacher: she knew about his problem and he often discussed this with her

behavior_patterns.condition: Discussing potential solutions for the bully character during the role-play debrief
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Admitted that apology was not easy for bullies as it threatened their ideal self-image
behavior_patterns.internal_state: Believed that by apologising he would show weakness and nobody would hold him in high esteem anymore
related_quotes: Apology would be the right thing to do in order to ﬁnd a way out of his problem but at the same time it would be a mistake since by apologising he would show weakness and nobody would hold him in high esteem anymore.
